original_question: Find new examples of hyperkahler manifolds.
target_in_paper: §1.2 (Examples), Question 1: Find new examples of hyperkähler manifolds. This is the specific open problem your draft is aiming at, rather than the broader boundedness conjecture in §1.5. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to complete: it matches Beauville’s Question 1 almost verbatim and correctly identifies the central object of the problem, namely hyperkähler manifolds. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is working in complex holomorphic-symplectic geometry, so hyperkähler here means a compact complex Kähler object in Beauville’s sense, not an arbitrary differential-geometric hyperkähler manifold. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))

To make the question stand-alone, one should spell out the paper’s implicit definition: a compact hyperkähler manifold is a compact simply connected Kähler manifold with H^0(X, Ω_X^*) = C[σ], where σ is an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic 2-form; Beauville also says these are irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))

The word new is relative to the examples listed immediately before Question 1: the Hilbert schemes S^[r] of length-r subschemes of a K3 surface, the generalized Kummer manifolds K_r(T) attached to a 2-dimensional complex torus T, and O’Grady’s exceptional examples in dimensions 6 and 10. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))

The surrounding discussion shows that constructions yielding only manifolds deformation equivalent to the standard S^[r] or K_r(T) series are not the sort of genuinely new examples Beauville is looking for. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))

Question 1 does not fix a dimension, impose projectivity or a polarization, or add numerical constraints; a faithful rewrite should not introduce such extra hypotheses. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))
refined_question: Construct a genuinely new compact simply connected Kähler manifold X over the complex numbers with H^0(X, Ω_X^*) = C[σ] for an everywhere nondegenerate holomorphic 2-form σ — equivalently, a compact hyperkähler (irreducible holomorphic symplectic) manifold in Beauville’s sense — such that X is not deformation equivalent to any of the known examples reviewed in §1.2: the Hilbert schemes S^[r] of points on K3 surfaces, the generalized Kummer manifolds K_r(T) associated with 2-dimensional complex tori, or O’Grady’s exceptional examples in dimensions 6 and 10. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Beauville’s Question 1 at the end of §1.2. The preceding context explains why this question is about scarcity of examples, not about period maps, cohomology, or boundedness: Beauville reviews the then-known constructions, notes that many apparently new moduli-space constructions turn out to be deformation equivalent to the standard K3^[r] or generalized Kummer families, and observes that hyperkähler desingularizations occur only in O’Grady’s two cases. That is the paper-specific sense in which one should sharpen new examples here. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4321.pdf))
